thesis: Modern digital infrastructure is unusually concentrated at two layers: cloud computing and advanced semiconductor production. AWS, Microsoft and Google dominate cloud infrastructure spending, while ASML and TSMC occupy critical positions in the equipment and manufacturing chain behind advanced chips.

facts.claim: In Q2 2026, AWS held 28% of worldwide cloud infrastructure services revenue, Microsoft 20%, and Google 15%.
AWS, Microsoft and Google together represented 63% of worldwide cloud infrastructure services revenue in Q2 2026.
ASML describes itself as a leading innovator in the global semiconductor ecosystem whose lithography portfolio enables microchip scaling.
ASML says DUV lithography systems are industry workhorses that produce the majority of layers in microchips.
TSMC manufactured 12,682 products using 305 technologies for 534 customers in 2025 across HPC, smartphones, IoT, automotive and consumer electronics.
TSMC reported that it accounted for 40% of its expanded Foundry 2.0 industry definition in 2025, up from 34% in 2024.

verified_numbers.context: Q2 2026 worldwide cloud infrastructure shares for AWS, Microsoft and Google respectively.
Q2 2026 enterprise spending on cloud infrastructure services reported by Synergy Research Group.
ASML 2025 system sales: 48 EUV, 279 DUV, and 208 metrology and inspection systems.
TSMC share of its Foundry 2.0 industry definition in 2025.

timeline.event: TSMC manufactured 12,682 products for 534 customers and reported 40% of its Foundry 2.0 industry definition.
ASML reported 535 system sales across EUV, DUV, metrology and inspection systems.
Worldwide cloud infrastructure spending reached $143 billion; AWS, Microsoft and Google held 28%, 20% and 15% shares.

sources.title: Q2 Cloud Market Passes $143 Billion; Highest Growth Rate in Eight Years

risk_flags: Frame these companies as critical infrastructure layers, not as secretly controlling the world.
Cloud market share and TSMC Foundry 2.0 share use different metrics and must not be compared directly.
